checks.name: a1-quota-budget-and-storage-ceilings
checks.summary: DefaultBudget=25,000/10,000/10,000 (50% of the Firestore free tier); DefaultStorageBudget{PayloadBytes:268,435,456,TotalBytes:536,870,912} added as a level, not reset at UTC midnight; each ceiling fails closed exactly one unit over the line (TestDailyBudgetFailsClosedExactlyOneOverTheLine, TestStorageBudgetFailsClosedExactlyOneOverTheLine); a zero or negative reservation is rejected (TestReserveRejectsNegativeOrZeroUsage, TestStorageLevelRejectsNegativeOrZeroDelta). All tests passed.

checks.name: a2-true-up-atomic-and-measured-capacity
checks.summary: quota.Counter.TrueUp corrects a prior worst-case Reserve to actual usage, clamped to [0,reserved] so it never goes below zero or above the pre-checked worst case (TestTrueUpNeverGoesBelowZeroOrAboveTheWorstCase); an over-budget worst case is refused before staging (TestReserveRefusesOverBudgetWorstCaseBeforeStaging); a small transaction commits only its actual cost (TestTrueUpCommitsOnlyActualCostOfASmallTransaction). Wired into internal/store/firestore unit.flush() before any Firestore write, using the size of the unit-of-work read cache for actual reads (every bounded-query read path now feeds that cache via countReads) and the number of staged writes for actual writes. Measured daily capacity at the 50% ceiling: worst-case-only 4 read-transactions per day (matches the documented pre-change figure) and 625 mutations per day; trued up to a single bounded page (1,002 actual reads) the read-transaction capacity rises to 24 per day (TestMeasuredDailyCapacityAtFiftyPercentCeiling).

checks.name: a3-quota-exhaustion-http-429
checks.summary: internal/api domainError maps quota.ErrOverBudget to HTTP 429 with error code quota_exhausted and a Retry-After header naming the next UTC midnight, instead of falling through to 400 invalid_request. The response body carries only the documented error, message, schema_version and correlation_id envelope fields, no usage figures.

checks.name: a5-preflight-ledger-approval-before-side-effect
checks.summary: internal/contracts CheckDeploymentPreflightLedger passes against the real repository state, where .agents/v2/preflight/ holds no files and the evidence index holds no gcp-live- component entry (TestDeploymentPreflightLedgerPassesWithNoRecords). Using temporary t.TempDir fixtures, auto-removed at test end, demonstrated all three required failures: a gcp-live- evidence entry with no matching preflight record (TestDeploymentPreflightLedgerFailsWithNoMatchingRecord), no artifact_refs entry naming deployment-preflight with a matching sha256 (TestDeploymentPreflightLedgerFailsWithNoArtifactRefMatch), and approval approved_at not strictly before observed_at (TestDeploymentPreflightLedgerFailsWithApprovalAfterObservation); plus the positive counterpart with a well-formed record (TestDeploymentPreflightLedgerPassesWithAWellFormedRecord). All 5 tests passed.

checks.name: a6-gitleaks-preflight-allowlist-positive-control
checks.summary: Extended the existing AND-scoped generic-api-key allowlist paths array with the literal path .agents/v2/preflight/.* (no second allowlist block added, condition stays AND). Measured before any change: a realistic minified deployment-preflight record with 64-hex image_digest and plan_digest committed under .agents/v2/preflight/ was already not flagged, 0 leaks, because none of the schema required field names contain generic-api-key trigger keywords; the explicit path entry documents and future-proofs this. Positive control 1, commit 23fdc65: a 64-hex value with a keyword field name outside every allowlisted path, result leaks found 1. Positive control 2, commit 3029b8d: a non-hex secret-shaped value inside .agents/v2/preflight/, result leaks found 2 cumulative, proving the AND condition still requires the value shape, not just the path. Probe files removed in commit 6192118. Raw branch HEAD still reports leaks found 2 because gitleaks git scans all reachable history and the probe-adding commits remain on this branch pending the coordinator squash merge, see a15 for the git commit-tree isolation proof that the integrated tree is clean.

checks.name: a7-infra-policy-fail-closed-budget-assertions
checks.summary: Replaced the single rg alternation, Shards=32 or Reads:40_000 or Writes:16_000 or Deletes:16_000, which passed if any one branch matched, with 8 independent fail-closed assertions: Shards, Reads, Writes, Deletes, PayloadBytes, TotalBytes, reconcile_schedule default, plus the pre-existing boundary-reservation and scheduler-cost-gate checks. Each of the 6 new value assertions was proven to bind by mutating exactly that value in a throwaway edit and confirming scripts/infra-policy.sh failed with a message naming that specific value, then restoring the original text and confirming make infra-policy passed again.

checks.name: a8-drift-detailed-exitcode-and-reproducible-plan-digest
checks.summary: scripts/infra-drift.sh now runs tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode so drift, exit 2, fails the script instead of being printed and ignored. scripts/infra-plan.sh additionally writes infra/build/infra.plan.json via tofu show -json and prints its sha256 so the digest a human approves is reproducible. Both scripts still refuse to run without a readable TFVARS_FILE, and now additionally fail closed with an explicit message when TF_STATE_BUCKET is unset. Measured: with TFVARS_FILE readable and TF_STATE_BUCKET unset, both scripts printed the message naming TF_STATE_BUCKET and exited 2. No tofu apply and no real GCP project were used; this is a local-only fail-closed check.

The apply step now applies the saved plan produced by the plan step, tofu apply -input=false build/infra.tfplan, after asserting via jq and sha256sum that the plan own sha256 equals target.plan_digest of the preflight record named by vars.GCP_PREFLIGHT_RECORD, and that record carries an approval object; any mismatch or missing record exits 1 before tofu apply runs. actionlint reported no errors on either workflow.

checks.name: a12-workflow-pins-uniqueness-check
checks.summary: scripts/workflow-pins.sh asserts that across .github/workflows the mapping from owner-repo and version comment to pinned sha is unique; wired into the Makefile workflow-pins target, which make check now runs. Passed with 3 unique owner-repo, version to sha pins, no disagreement. Proved it binds by temporarily reintroducing the mistyped jetify-com devbox-install-action revision in deploy.yml: the script failed naming the disagreement; restoring the correct pin made it pass again. actionlint alone cannot detect this class of defect because it validates workflow syntax, not whether a pinned revision exists upstream or agrees with another workflow pinning the same version.

checks.name: a13-firestore-emulator-quota-integration
checks.summary: scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -race ./internal/store/firestore passed, including three new tests: TestQuotaTrueUpCommitsAtomicallyWithCallerMutation, the trued-up quota total commits in the same transaction as the caller mutation and is far below the worst-case reservation; TestQuotaOverBudgetTransactionLeavesNoPartialMutation, a worst-case reservation over budget is refused before flush and the caller staged mutation is never persisted; and TestQuotaDiscardedAttemptContributesNothingToARetry, a callback that reserves worst-case usage and then errors out before flush, modelling what Firestore does to a callback attempt it aborts and retries, leaves no trace, and a fresh attempt for the same key commits only its own trued-up cost. Emulator success is evidence about this adapter transaction wiring only; it is never reported as verification of real Firestore, real contention, or real IAM, which remains V2-014 scope.
